title: 390. Geometry, Spatial Thinking & Measurement: Cross Sections of Solids
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the shape of an interior face-parallel cube section.
questions.question: A plane cuts a cube strictly between two opposite faces and is parallel to those faces. What shape is the cross section?
questions.explanation: Each of the four side faces contributes a segment equal to a cube edge. Adjacent segments are perpendicular, giving a square.
questions.hint: Trace the intersections of the plane with the side faces.

questions.learningObjective: Identify a cylinder section made perpendicular to its axis.
questions.question: A plane cuts a right circular cylinder strictly between its bases and is perpendicular to the cylinder's axis. What shape is the cross section?
questions.explanation: The plane is parallel to the circular bases. Its intersection consists of a circular disk whose boundary is a circle of the base radius.
questions.hint: Relate the cutting plane's direction to the base planes.

questions.learningObjective: Use a right triangle to find a spherical section's radius.
questions.question: A sphere has radius \(5\text{ cm}\). A plane is at perpendicular distance \(3\text{ cm}\) from its center. What is the radius of the circular cross section?
questions.explanation: If the section radius is \(s\), then \(s^2+3^2=5^2\). Thus \(s^2=16\), giving \(s=4\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Join the sphere center to the section center and a point on its boundary.

questions.concept: Cone section measured from the base
questions.learningObjective: Convert a section height into an apex-based similarity ratio.
questions.question: A right circular cone has height \(12\text{ cm}\) and base radius \(6\text{ cm}\). A plane parallel to its base lies \(4\text{ cm}\) above the base. What is the cross-section radius?
questions.explanation: The plane is \(8\text{ cm}\) below the apex. Similarity gives radius \(6\cdot\frac{8}{12}=4\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Measure the section's distance from the apex, not only from the base.

questions.concept: Parallel section of a square pyramid
questions.learningObjective: Scale a square section using its apex-based height.
questions.question: A square pyramid has height \(10\text{ cm}\) and base side \(8\text{ cm}\). A plane parallel to the base is \(5\text{ cm}\) below the apex. What is the side length of its square cross section?
questions.explanation: The linear ratio is \(\frac{5}{10}=\frac{1}{2}\), so the section side is \(8\cdot\frac{1}{2}=4\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Parallel pyramid sections are similar to the base.

questions.concept: Horizontal section of a rectangular prism
questions.learningObjective: Preserve base dimensions in a parallel prism section.
questions.question: A right rectangular prism has base dimensions \(8\text{ cm}\) by \(6\text{ cm}\) and height \(5\text{ cm}\). A plane parallel to the base cuts it halfway up its height. What are the section's side lengths?
questions.explanation: A right prism's parallel sections retain the base dimensions. The halfway height does not halve either base side, so the lengths are \(8\) and \(6\text{ centimeters}\).
questions.hint: Compare a prism's side edges with a pyramid's converging edges.

questions.concept: Oblique cube section through adjacent vertices
questions.learningObjective: Classify a coordinate-defined triangular cube section.
questions.question: The cube is \(0\le x,y,z\le4\). A plane passes through \((4,0,0)\), \((0,4,0)\), and \((0,0,4)\). Which description fits its cross section?
questions.explanation: The plane is \(x+y+z=4\). Within the cube its section is the triangle with the three stated vertices. Each pair is at distance \(\sqrt{4^2+4^2}=4\sqrt{2}\), so it is equilateral.
questions.hint: Find the plane's intercepts and compare the three joining lengths.

questions.learningObjective: Determine dimensions of a plane section containing a cylinder axis.
questions.question: A right circular cylinder has radius \(3\text{ cm}\) and height \(8\text{ cm}\). A plane contains its entire axis. What is the cross section?
questions.explanation: The plane cuts each base along a diameter of length \(6\text{ cm}\). The other dimension is the cylinder height, \(8\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Examine where an axis-containing plane meets the two circular bases.

questions.concept: Area of an offset spherical section
questions.learningObjective: Find a section radius before computing its area.
questions.question: A sphere has radius \(13\text{ cm}\). A plane is at distance \(5\text{ cm}\) from its center. What is the area of the circular cross section?
questions.explanation: The squared section radius is \(13^2-5^2=144\). Therefore the circular area is \(144\pi\text{ cm}^2\), smaller than a central section.
questions.hint: An offset section does not use the full sphere radius.

questions.learningObjective: Identify and measure a triangle cut from a coordinate tetrahedron.
questions.question: A tetrahedron has vertices \((0,0,0)\), \((6,0,0)\), \((0,6,0)\), and \((0,0,6)\). What is the area of its section by \(x+y+z=3\)?
questions.explanation: The section vertices are \((3,0,0)\), \((0,3,0)\), and \((0,0,3)\). Its equilateral side is \(3\sqrt{2}\). The area is \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}(3\sqrt{2})^2=\frac{9\sqrt{3}}{2}\).
questions.hint: Find the plane's intersections with the three edges from the origin.
